title: Where are y'all getting players?
author: spotwork
selftext: Are y'all just making games for funsies? Or are you throwing them on a store and hoping someone notices them? Or are you dropping more cash on marketing? What about playtesting? Doing that at all? Where are you getting people to play it?

comments.author: Every-Prize4720
comments.body: most games fail and slowly die out. either money gets you players or word of mouth.

comments.author: final_boss_editing
comments.body: Been just using organic to see the promise of game experiments and then the ones that look good I test more growth stuff

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body: I just post on reddit mostly. it sort of helped but not really

comments.author: wewerecreaturres
comments.body: I’d guess most successful ones get with a publisher. And if a publisher won’t take you, probs a good sign your game isn’t good

replies.author: UnderStrangeStars
replies.body:
This is very bad advice. A publisher usually only wants to get involved when you have > 100,000 (on the low end) Wishlist adds or you're a team with a proven track record.

Making and marketing a good game are very difficult... and take a ton of time and research.

comments.author: TimeWasterHQ
comments.body: Twitter and Reddit seem to work the best. I think when you see someone give you the background and context to why+how they made the game, it really does peak interest more

comments.author: CrispyOwl717
comments.body: IRL: Uber Drivers, People at Bars, Technical/Gaming Meetups (like Smash Bros Tournaments or AI/Crypto meetups) -> Online: TikTok, Reddit, Instagram Reels, YouTube

comments.author: Affectionate_Fact854
comments.body:
I used to drop everything I make on ichio 
But recently I tested dropping playable versions on actual monetized html sites like crazygames 

Fun fact 
The same games I had on ichio for 6 months has recieved 5x that views and plays in a question of 1 week 

:) 

Only when I find a game that really sparks on playgama/crazygames  will I even consider gambling 100$ to make a steam release.

replies.author: Lextrot
replies.body: What stage in development do you post your games? Are they like demos or short "GameJam-ish" complete games? How long do you usually work on a title before moving on to another to see what works?

replies.author: Affectionate_Fact854
replies.body:
First title I worked on took me 2 years to learn the engine, learn to optimize and to redo the art style and drawings 2 times 
(Currently it averages people playing it roughly 30minutes per session and it receives roughly 50 daily players) that's sad I know..  

The second launched title took me 2weeks ( play sessions is roughly 6minutes, but it rakes in roughly 340 daily players) 

But currently working on balancing a incremental game( took me 4weeks) 
And also preparing the 4th games mechanics 

Also (games I do upload , I still give monthly updates)

I would say I usually do 1week prototype with basic concepts before I decide if it shows any value to continue 

If it passes week 1, I'll give it another week, and after is when I decide if it's worth uploading and giving continued development


Biggest lesson I learned was 
Don't invest to much time on a single project unless it truly shows promising feedback
